title: The third
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The third. The box opened. The fireworks laid out on the counter in order of the uncle's choosing: he points, Gully lays. The last one is set apart. The red one. The strip draws it gray with a circle around it.

panels.composition: The shack. The box open. GULLY laying fireworks on the counter in a row. The UNCLE in the door in the chair, pointing. WOOD, BARNABY.

image.prompt: a teenager laying fireworks in a row on a bait shack counter as an old man in a lawn chair in the doorway points, a young man and a dog watching, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The row: tubes, cones, a cake. In order. The uncle's order.

image.prompt: close on a row of fireworks laid on a wooden counter in careful order, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The last one, set apart. A single tube. The uncle's finger. 'That one last.'

image.prompt: close on a single firework tube set apart from the row with an old finger pointing at it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The counter with the row and the one apart. Wood drawing it: all gray, and a circle drawn around the last. The strip can't do red. It can do a circle.

image.prompt: a young man drawing a row of fireworks on a counter, his drawing showing them all gray with a circle drawn around the last one, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The red one, set apart, circled. The strip can do a circle.
